title: Invitation To Death
paragraphs: By the time Father and the sister disappeared into the castle, the slaves suddenly stopped playing and sat down. Did they become uneasy after the sister left? Where did all that energy from earlier go?
“What’s wrong?”
Sakura-chan and Yuki-chan asked.
“Are you scared of people?”
The slaves shook their heads.
“It’s okay… Everyone feels safe because of Sakura-chan, Yuki-chan, the Shield Hero, and Sadeena-oneesan.”
“Then why aren’t you playing?”
“Because Sadeena-oneesan… is pretending to be fine, and we don’t want to worry her…”
“Sadeena-oneesan is acting fine, but she’s probably crying inside…”
“Yeah. She’s sad because she couldn’t save everyone.”
Oh, even the village slaves noticed what Father had already realized. I had no idea at all.
“Do you not want to play?”
“We want to, but we’re more worried about Sadeena-oneesan. So, we tried too hard in front of her… and now we’re tired and want to rest.”

Even the children are carrying such burdens. The Filolials have said that the sister was someone they could always rely on in the village. That’s exactly why the slaves were acting cheerful, so they wouldn’t worry her. And that’s why they’re now exhausted. Acting cheerful is difficult, after all.
“Then how about sitting and talking?”
“Yeah. We can do that much.”
“Then I shall tell you stories of Motoyasu-sama and the heroes’ heroic exploits.”
Yuki-chan began recounting past events to the resting slaves in the form of stories. Gradually, I started to hear a livelier atmosphere. But… it seems I’m not needed here.
“Should I go help Father? I could use magic to warm the room so the sister can rest comfortably.”
“Yes… please go help the Shield Hero.”
The village slave nodded. I’ve been entrusted with the task.
“Well then, I’ll be off. Yuki-chan, Sakura-chan, make sure to keep the stories going.”
“We’ve only just begun!”
Yuki-chan and Sakura-chan were happily narrating to the slaves, looking very pleased.

Is this what they call an epic tale sung by bards? Filolials do love singing, after all. Ah, this reminds me of Filo-tan’s idol shows. With those thoughts in mind, I followed after Father and the others. I arrived at the room where the sister was being put to bed.
Should I knock?
“Sadeena-san, why don’t you take better care of yourself?!”
I heard Father’s voice. It sounded like they were arguing. Should I go in? Or should I wait quietly? It feels like I missed the right moment.
“Oh… I’m fine, really. Naofumi-chan, go back to everyone quickly. I’ll be okay.”
I could hear her carefree voice, but it was immediately followed by a fit of coughing.
“…Hey, Sadeena-san. I think you’re a very kind and strong person. Despite having the power to loop through time, you never blamed Motoyasu-kun for ignoring Raphtalia-chan. Instead, you accepted him.”
Oh? Am I being put in the spotlight here? Indeed, the sister’s reaction was perfectly normal.

“Even though you must feel anger toward us… toward the country and the world, you never complain or express resentment. I think that’s something truly admirable. But Sadeena-san, please show your emotions more… No matter how much you scold me, I’m prepared to take it.”
“Naofumi-chan…”

The sister’s usually cheerful tone had completely faded. I’ve completely missed my timing here. If I were to go in now, Father would probably glare at me for not reading the mood. But I’m going in anyway. I tried to turn the doorknob, but it wouldn’t budge.
What’s going on? Is Father holding it from the inside? Or is it locked?
“Hey… Sadeena-san, you can’t really be laughing about Raphtalia-chan’s safety, can you?”
“To you, Raphtalia-chan comes first, followed by the village children. I know that. Do you think I don’t realize the swirling emotions you’re holding back because we couldn’t save them?”
I heard the sound of Father stepping closer to the sister, his footsteps heavy.
“And yet, you kept it all bottled up… I arrogantly assumed that was your way of being considerate. But it’s okay to be angry. If you could just lash out at me, I would…”
At that moment, the sister let out a light cough.
“…Even if I resented you, Raphtalia-chan, her parents, and the villagers wouldn’t come back,” the sister responded in a calm voice I had never heard from her before.
“And besides, taking it out on Naofumi-chan and the others would just be a cowardly excuse. That’s wrong. Even if the Four Holy Heroes, who are said to be saviors of the world, couldn’t save them.”
“Sadeena-san…”

“I’m the one who couldn’t save Raphtalia-chan’s parents. And I couldn’t protect Raphtalia-chan or the villagers either… Even though I had enough strength to protect them all, they still slipped through my fingers…”

Come to think of it, even in the first world, Father had said that the sister was by far the strongest among the village slaves. And yet, her village was destroyed. There must have been many reasons behind that.
“I did want someone like Naofumi-chan to buy up all the village children in Melromarc.”
“I understand that…”
“But… blaming Naofumi-chan and the others for not being able to save Raphtalia-chan won’t change anything. It was all because of my own poor choices.”
The sister’s coughing sounded worse than before.
“Naofumi-chan, Raphtalia-chan and her parents… they were my reason for living.”
“Sadeena-san! B-Blood!?”
I could sense Father casting magic. It’s probably healing magic.
“Liberation Heal X! Ugh… The bleeding stopped, but…”

“During the first wave, I couldn’t protect Raphtalia-chan’s parents. No, when the wave struck, I was too far away to get there in time. Things had been too peaceful before that… I must have let my guard down.”
“That’s…”
Father seemed at a loss for words. I recall hearing in the first world that the waves were like natural disasters. Even in this loop, everyone seems to think of them that way.
…But something feels off. If that’s true, then why are there enemies claiming to be gods? It’s the same question that arose when Father and I fought reincarnators and otherworlders.
“…But when I finally returned to the village after several days, there was no one left.”
“…Yeah. Eclair-san said that aside from the damage caused by the wave, the kingdom’s soldiers conducted a slave raid on the territory. It was truly horrible.”

“I searched desperately. I prayed they were still alive. But I couldn’t get close to the darkness in this country. So, I went to Zeltoble, where they specialize in dealing with slaves, and became a combat slave to search for them. I thought that with enough money, I could do something because of the large connections there.”
“That’s quite a detour, but… it couldn’t be helped.”

“This illness… it’s the punishment I bear. That’s why, even if Naofumi-chan and the others give me medicine, I can’t be cured… It’s the punishment… the curse for not being able to save Raphtalia-chan and her parents.”
“That’s not…”
Should I just break down the door already? But I have a feeling Father would be mad at me if I did. As I was thinking that, something flashed through my mind.
I thought I saw a vision of Filo-tan, beckoning me. If I don’t save the sister… does that mean I won’t be able to see Filo-tan again?
As I was being distracted by that illusion, I heard a noise from inside the room. I heard the sister’s weak coughing, followed by a loud thud, as if someone had stomped or punched the ground.
“So, Naofumi-chan and the others don’t need to worry about me… I’m already…”
At that moment, the sister suddenly opened the door and pushed Father out.
“Oh?”
“Oh my?”
The sister and I locked eyes. Then, Father stood up and positioned himself in front of me. What’s going on?
“…Motoyasu-kun!”
“Yes, indeed!”

Ah, I recognize this. It’s that expression Father makes when he’s about to scold me for not acting sooner. He’s probably trying to spur me into action because I’ve been too slow. Father grabbed both of my shoulders. I’ll steel myself.
“Motoyasu-kun, I’m sorry… I’ll apologize as many times as it takes. What I’m about to say is incredibly selfish, emotional, and arrogant… but I need to ask you for a favor.”
“W-What is it?”
Father, with a face that looked like he was about to cry, pleaded with me. This reaction was completely different from anything I’d seen before. This wasn’t a scolding… it was something else.
“Right now… kill me and restart the loop.”
